properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. @ajs, 2026-09-24, first about flo2's new users and then about reflow2 itself:

"I was thinking that we some how have to create a cheat sheet for new users ... to explain what skills you can use and how to use it. So far, my brother Seth figured out only because I told him what to do and it was only the genesis, but I don't think he'll know anything beyond /genesis. So I'd imagine to him, he's probably like, cool, I created a design, so what now?"

"reflow2 has some skills because the same problem also affects reflow2 at the lower level for users using reflow2 like I am here."

WHAT EXISTS, AND THE HOLE BETWEEN THEM:
- `help` (/what-is-this) answers WHERE DO I START: /genesis, /adopt or /where by situation, then every skill from `list_skills`. It is written for before a design exists.
- `find_skills` answers WHAT IS THAT SKILL CALLED, for someone who already knows the job they want done (req:a-skill-is-reachable-from-a-description-of-the-job-in-a-persons-words).
- NOTHING answers "I HAVE A DESIGN, WHAT CAN I DO NOW?" — the moment right after /genesis. genesis ends on a gap round and `loop_status`, and the closing words that follow are drawn from `loop_status`'s `next`, written for the agent in reflow2's nouns (fact:root-cause-the-lens-rode-the-skill-rail-and-the-closing-words-are-chosen-on-the-loop-rail).
- The owner of reflow2 forgets his own skills ("I continually forget which skills are available"). If he does, a newcomer who was told one command will not find the rest.

═══ OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN ═══

(a) "WHAT NEXT" AT THE END OF A SKILL. A skill's closing words name two or three things the person can say next, in their terms, e.g. "/gaps to see what is still open, /req to add something it needs, /where to see where it stands". Start with genesis and adopt, the two that create a design.
- SMALL: a closing paragraph per skill, or one shared rule every skill's ending follows.
- It serves Claude Code users and every flo2 chat user at once, because flo2 serves these skills unchanged.

(b) A "NOW YOU HAVE A DESIGN" TIER IN /what-is-this. After "where do I start", a short everyday set of about five skills (/where, /gaps, /req, /brainstorm, /jot), then "everything else: list_skills or /find-skills".
- SMALL: help's text.

(c) A DERIVED EVERYDAY SET. Rather than a hand-picked five, a marker on each skill (e.g. an `everyday` flag beside `audience`) that help, flo2's cheat sheet and any menu all read. MEDIUM: build.rs, list_skills and every skill's frontmatter. It does keep the five from drifting in three places.

(d) A PERSON-FACING "WHAT YOU CAN DO NEXT" IN loop_status, beside the agent-facing `next`. MEDIUM, and it collides with the lens work on closing words.

═══ PUSHBACK, RECORDED BESIDE IT ═══
· A SUGGESTION AFTER EVERY SKILL BECOMES NOISE for someone who knows the skills. Limiting it to genesis and adopt, or to a design with few captures, keeps it where it teaches.
· A HAND-PICKED FIVE WILL BE PICKED DIFFERENTLY IN THREE PLACES (help, flo2's cheat sheet, a menu) unless one record owns it, which is the argument for (c) and against copying a list.
· NAMING SKILLS BY SLASH COMMAND ASSUMES A PERSON CAN TYPE ONE. In Claude Code that is true; in a chat app it depends on flo2 resolving the word (it does) and, on Grok, on "use flo2" being said first.

THE flo2 HALF (a cheat sheet on flo2.io, a welcome at sign-up, the chat app's own menu) is recorded in flo2's design as dec:idea-a-new-person-learns-what-they-can-do-after-genesis. That one depends on this one: flo2 serves reflow2's skills unchanged, so whatever reflow2 says at the end of genesis, flo2's users hear too.
